To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new program, ORPHEUS, accurately predicts gene starts and gene complements in sequenced bacterial genomes.
ORPHEUS predicts gene starts with high accuracy and is applicable to completely sequenced bacterial chromosomes.

the combination of diverse evidence for gene identification and gene start prediction in completely sequenced genomes leads to high gene prediction accuracy, and that the ORPHEUS program is a powerful tool for gene identification in newly sequenced genomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
gene prediction in bacterial genomes.
the analysis of protein-coding gene sequences.
the development of a new program that combines diverse sources of evidence for gene recognition and provides accurate gene start prediction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the program is very useful for gene recognition in bacterial genomes.

the ORPHEUS program is able to correctly identify most of the genes in a bacterial genome, including the exact gene start, in a large majority of cases, and is therefore a valuable addition to the existing gene-finding programs.
ORPHEUS predicts gene structures and gene start sites with a high accuracy and reliability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ORPHEUS is a very useful tool for gene recognition in bacterial genomes.
ORPHEUS is a reliable tool for gene recognition and gene start prediction in completely sequenced genomes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of different evidence types, including similarity search and statistical analysis, is necessary for accurate gene identification in completely sequenced genomes.

a combination of different evidence sources, including a similarity search against protein databases and a search for ribosome-binding sites, leads to a high accuracy of gene identification and prediction of N-termini.

the use of a large set of diverse data sources and statistical characteristics of protein coding regions and ribosome binding sites allows us to predict gene complements in bacterial genomes with high accuracy.   1
